chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Musa ibn al-Qasim said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him): 'I intend to perform Tawaf on your behalf and on behalf of your father.' I was told: 'The successors (Imams) are not Tawafed for.' He said: 'Yes, perform Tawaf as much as you can, for that is permissible.'

Then, three years later, I said to him: 'I had asked your permission to perform Tawaf on your behalf and on behalf of your father, and you granted it to me, so I performed Tawaf for both of you as God willed. Then something occurred to my heart, so I acted upon it.'
He said: 'And what was it?' I said: 'One day I performed Tawaf on behalf of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).' He said three times: 'May God bless the Messenger of God.'

The second day on behalf of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Then I performed Tawaf on the third day on behalf of al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and on the fourth day on behalf of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and on the fifth day on behalf of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), and on the sixth day on behalf of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), and on the seventh day on behalf of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), and on the eighth day on behalf of your father Musa (peace be upon him), and on the ninth day on behalf of your father Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him), and on the tenth day on behalf of you, O my master.

And these are the ones for whom I affirm God's guardianship (Wilayah). He said: 'Then, by God, you affirm God with the religion that He accepts from the servants and does not accept any other than it.'
I said: 'And sometimes I performed Tawaf on behalf of your mother Fatimah (peace be upon her), and sometimes I did not.' He said: 'Increase in this, for it is the best of what you do, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform Tawaf on behalf of the Imams in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential validity of *Tawaf al-Nawafil* performed on behalf of the Imams, a practice rooted in the concept of *Wilayah* (divine guardianship). Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation that this act constitutes the 'religion He accepts' underscores its theological weight as an expression of devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt, while the narrator’s detailed enumeration of the Twelve Imams highlights the continuity of spiritual authority. Scholarly tradition views this as a precursor to the widespread Shia practice of dedicating ritual acts to the Imams to seek their intercession and emulate their status.
